subject.title: Abort does not reap spawned child `claude -p` processes — orphaned agent keeps executing with bypassPermissions

question: Which detached processes launched during an agent turn are autonomous executors that explicit user abort must terminate, versus intentional background jobs that may survive?
rationale: Current main deliberately preserves registered background exec sessions, but the reported privileged autonomous survivor violates the operator-visible stop boundary; implementation cannot safely infer this distinction from descendant PIDs after detachment.

options.title: Contain autonomous executors
options.body: Require autonomous agent runners to remain in a turn-owned process scope that explicit abort terminates, while ordinary registered background jobs keep their current behavior.

options.title: Register visible survivors
options.body: Allow detached autonomous work to survive only through a typed background-task API that remains listed and operator-controllable after abort.

options.title: Block unsupported detachment
options.body: Reject or prominently warn on privileged daemonization patterns when OpenClaw cannot retain lifecycle ownership.

recommendation.title: Contain autonomous executors
recommendation.body: Require autonomous agent runners to remain in a turn-owned process scope that explicit abort terminates, while ordinary registered background jobs keep their current behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant chat-abort and background-survival contracts originate in this person's commits, making them the strongest available owner for reconciling the boundary.
